 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
At Gwalior

Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Ashish Shroti

On The 2 nd Of April, 2026
 Misc. Appeal No. 275 of 2012
 Smt.Shanno And Others
 Versus
 M/S Amit Gas Service Through Properieter Pokhan (Died)
 Thr. Lrs Manoj Dhaureliya And Others
 Appearance:
 Smt. Meena Singhal - Advocate for the appellants
 Shri Ram Vilas Sharma- Advocate for respondent no. 3/In
Company.

Order 
This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, is filed by the appellants, being dissatisfied with the award dated 22/11/2011, passed by learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Gwalior (M.P.), in Claim Case No.131/2012 by which the learned Claims Tribunal awarded a total sum of Rs.5,16,000/- with interest @ 9% per annum to the appellants/claimants by way of compensation for the death of one Sushil alias Kallu, husband of appellant no.1, father of appellant no.2, 3 & 7, brother of appellant no.5 & 6 and son of appellant no.4 in a road accident dated 13/11/2010.
2.

The brief facts of the claim petition are that on 13/11/10 when deceased Sushil alias Kalu was going on motorcycle No. M.H.31/D.H.8403 along with his maternal uncle from Moti Jheel to Bahodapur, it is alleged NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:11107 2 MA-275-2012 that Sushil parked his motorcycle near Sudarshan Petrol Pump and was talking with some persons then respondent no.2, driving vehicle No. M.P.07 /G 3986 at a high speed rashly and negligently hit motorcycle as a result of which Kalu alias Sushil sitting on the motorcycle fell on the ground.
The wheel of the offending vehicle passed over his body as a result of which he sustained grievous injuries.
He was taken to hospital in an ambulance, however, he died on the way.
The report of the accident was lodged by Ballu alias Maniram at P.S. Bahodapura.

3. According to claimants, the compensation awarded by the learned Tribunal is on lower side,
hence needs to be enhanced.

4. It is not necessary to narrate the entire facts in detail, such as how the accident occurred, who was negligent in driving the offending vehicle, who is liable for paying compensation etc.
It is for the reason that all these findings are recorded in favour of claimants by the Tribunal which are not under challenge.
In this view of the matter, there is no justification to burden the judgment by detailing facts on all these issues.

5. As observed supra, it is a death case in which due to injuries sustained in road accident dated 13/11/2010, one Susil alias Kallu succumbed to the same while he was on the way to hospital in an ambulance.

Therefore, his mother, wife, siblings and children (collectively referred as 'claimants')

sentences.text: 5. Learned Claims Tribunal after issuing summons and recording evidence and after appreciating the same, passed the impugned award.

Learned Tribunal after assessing the income of deceased to be Rs.3,000/- per month, deducted 1/4th towards self expenditure and applying multiplier of 18 and thus awarded a total sum of Rs.5,16,000/- to the claimants towards compensation.
6. Learned counsel for the appellants submitted that the Claims Tribunal erred in determining the income of the deceased at Rs.3,000/- per month only, instead of Rs.10,000/- per month.

She referred to the testimony of AW/1- Smt. Shanno (wife of deceased), AW/2- Ballu alias Maniram and AW/3- Jandel Singh to say that they have categorically stated that monthly income of the deceased was Rs.10,000/-.
Their testimony remained unrebutted even in the cross-examination.

She thus submitted that in absence of any contrary evidence, the oral statement given by the aforesaid three witnesses ought to have been accepted and the income of the deceased should have been taken to be at Rs.10,000/- per month.
Enhancement of impugned compensation is also sought on the ground that the Tribunal failed to award compensation towards future prospects and other conventional heads.
It is further submitted that the dependency has also been wrongly assessed by the Claims Tribunal at 1/4th instead of 1/5th looking to the number of dependents.

7. Learned counsel for respondent no.3/Insurance Company opposed NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:11107 4 MA-275-2012 the prayer.
He submitted that the income of the deceased cannot be determined solely based upon the oral testimony of the witnesses.
He submitted that the deceased was stated to be running a tea stall at bus stand, if that be so, there has to be some documents in support of his business.
However, no such document has admittedly been produced before the Tribunal.
He further argued that AW/2 and AW/3 were not connected with the family of deceased and were therefore, not supposed to know about the income of the deceased.
He thus submitted that income of the deceased has rightly been determined by the Tribunal.
He also denied that appellants claim for future prospects, dependency and other heads.

8. Considered the arguments and perused the record.

2 9. Appellants claims that the income of the deceased was Rs.10,000/- per month.
This claim has been based upon oral testimony of AW/1, AW/2 & AW/3.
However, the income could not have been determined based solely upon the oral testimony when the appellants could have produced the documentary evidence in support of the same.
If the deceased was running a tea stall near bus stand, he must be having relevant documents viz. license etc. issued by the Municipal Corporation in this regard.
Further, AW/3- Jandel Singh is stated to be one of the customers of the deceased and thus was not supposed to know about his income.
Similarly, AW/2- Ballu alias Maniram is stated to be uncle (Mama) of the deceased and was not residing with the family of the deceased.
Thus, his testimony is also not acceptable for purpose of determination of income of deceased.

10. From perusal of the record as well as findings as recorded in the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:11107 5 MA-275-2012 impugned award, in the opinion of this Court the income of deceased as assessed by the Claims Tribunal is on lower side.
His income should be Rs.4,145/- per month, as minimum remuneration of a unskilled person as was prevailing on the date of accident as per SALSA Guidelines.
The multiplier of 18, as applied by the Claims Tribunal is just and proper.

As regards deduction towards personal expenses to the extent of 1/4th, appears to be on higher side,
therefore, looking to the number of dependents, which are seven in the present case, deducting towards self dependency would be applicable to the extent of 1/5th in light of decision of Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation, reported in (2006)9 SCC 121.

sentences.text:
Further,
this Court is also of the opinion that the appellants are entitled to get amount towards future prospects.

Thus, an addition of 40% of actual income of deceased towards future prospects is required to be added in light of decision of Apex Court in the matter of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and Ors., reported in (2017)16 SCC 680 .

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and Ors., reported in (2017)16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: They are also entitled to get amount towards consortium.

11. Thus, by assessing monthly income of deceased at Rs.4,145/- per month, his yearly income comes to Rs.49,740/- to which 1/5th is required to be deducted towards personal expenses and after deducting the same, remaining amount comes to Rs.39,792/-.
Adding 40% as future prospects, the income comes to Rs.39,792/- + 15,916/- = 55,708/-.
Multiplier of 18 is required to be applied and after applying the same, the compensation to which claimants are entitled for under the head loss of dependency comes to Rs.10,02,744/-.
Rs.30,000/- is required to be added towards funeral expenses NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:11107 6 MA-275-2012 and loss of estate.
An amount of Rs.2,80,000/- (40,000/- each) is required to be added towards loss of consortium.
Thus, the total compensation amount comes to Rs.10,02,744/- + Rs.30,000 + Rs.2,80,000/- = Rs.13,12,744/-.

The Claims Tribunal has already awarded a compensation of Rs.5,16,000/- therefore, claimants are held entitled to receive an enhanced compensation of Rs.7,96,744/- which shall carry interest @ 6% per annum from the date of claim case and shall be payable to the claimants within two months from today.
Rest of the conditions including liability as imposed by Claims Tribunal shall remain intact.

12. Appeal stands allowed in part and impugned award is modified to the extent as indicated hereinabove.
(ASHISH SHROTI) JUDGE JPS/-
